tasks.title: Template string: a greeting
tasks.statement: Write a function greet(name) that returns the string «Привет, <name>!» (for example, «Привет, мир!»). Use a template string in backticks.
tasks.hint: return `Привет, ${name}!`;

tasks.title: console.log: three lines
tasks.statement: Write a function run() that prints three lines with console.log — «JavaScript», the number 42 and the value true — each in a separate call.
tasks.hint: console.log("JavaScript"); console.log(42); console.log(true);

tasks.title: Type of a value: null and arrays
tasks.statement: Write a function typeName(v) that returns a string with the name of the type, like typeof, but «null» for null and «array» for an array.
tasks.hint: First check for null and Array.isArray, then return typeof v.

tasks.title: How many falsy values
tasks.statement: Write a function countFalsy(arr) that returns how many elements of the array count as falsy when checked in a condition.
tasks.hint: if (!x) n++ — this is also right for 0n: it is falsy too.

tasks.title: A default value: only for null and undefined
tasks.statement: Write a function orDefault(x, d) that returns d only if x is null or undefined; for 0, the empty string and false it returns x itself. You must not use the || and && operators.
tasks.hint: The ?? operator picks the right side only for null and undefined.

tasks.title: A safe path: user?.profile?.name
tasks.statement: Write a function userName(user) that returns user.profile.name, and if null or undefined is met along the way, the string «аноним». Do not use if statements or the ternary ? : — ?. and ?? are enough.
tasks.hint: return user?.profile?.name ?? "аноним";

tasks.title: Money without the 0.30000000000000004 tail
tasks.statement: Write a function addMoney(a, b) that adds two amounts in rubles and kopecks and returns the result rounded to kopecks (two decimal places), so that 0.1 + 0.2 gives exactly 0.3.
tasks.hint: Math.round((a + b) * 100) / 100

tasks.title: A safe integer
tasks.statement: Write a function isSafe(n) that returns true if n is an integer whose absolute value does not exceed 2 to the power of 53 minus 1 (Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER). You must not use Number.isSafeInteger.
tasks.hint: Number.isInteger(n) and Math.abs(n) <= 2 ** 53 - 1; don't forget to check the type.

tasks.title: Equality that accounts for NaN
tasks.statement: Write a function sameValue(a, b) that returns true if a === b or if both values are NaN. You must not use Object.is.
tasks.hint: NaN is the only value not equal to itself: x !== x.

tasks.title: Factorial with BigInt
tasks.statement: Write a function factorial(n): n is an ordinary integer from 0 to 30; the function returns n! as a string that is exact for any n (use BigInt).
tasks.hint: Start with 1n, multiply by BigInt(i); the result is String(r).

tasks.title: How many characters in a string
tasks.statement: Write a function charCount(s) that returns the number of real characters in the string (an emoji counts as one), not UTF-16 units. A for-of loop or the spread operator will help.
tasks.hint: for (const ch of s) n++;

tasks.title: Reversing a string by characters
tasks.statement: Write a function reverse(s) that returns a string with the characters in reverse order; emoji must stay whole.
tasks.hint: [...s].reverse().join("")

tasks.title: A palindrome
tasks.statement: Write a function isPalindrome(s) that returns true if the string reads the same in both directions, ignoring case, spaces and punctuation (for example, «А роза упала на лапу Азора»).
tasks.hint: toLowerCase, then replace(/[^\p{L}\p{N}]/gu, "") and compare with the reversed string.

tasks.title: Each word capitalized
tasks.statement: Write a function titleCase(s): words are separated by a single space; in each word the first letter becomes uppercase and the rest lowercase.
tasks.hint: split(" "), for each word slice(0, 1).toUpperCase() + slice(1).toLowerCase(), then join.

tasks.title: Vowels in Russian text
tasks.statement: Write a function countVowels(s) that counts the Russian vowel letters «а, е, ё, и, о, у, ы, э, ю, я» in any case.
tasks.hint: "аеёиоуыэюя".includes(ch) for each character of the lowercased string.

tasks.title: Template: name and age
tasks.statement: Write a function formatUser(name, age) that returns a string like «Ада (36)». You must not join with the + operator — use a template string.
tasks.hint: return `${name} (${age})`;

tasks.title: Truncating a string with an ellipsis
tasks.statement: Write a function truncate(s, n): if the length of s is at most n, return s; otherwise return the first n - 1 characters and «…». The length of the result is always at most n.
tasks.hint: s.length <= n ? s : s.slice(0, n - 1) + "…"

tasks.title: Fix it: const and a sum
tasks.statement: The function sumAll should return the sum of the numbers in an array, but it fails with TypeError: Assignment to constant variable. Fix the declaration.
tasks.hint: The accumulated value changes, so declare it with let.

tasks.title: Fix it: for…in instead of for…of
tasks.statement: The function sumAll2 should sum the values of an array, but instead it joins its indexes into a string. Fix the loop.
tasks.hint: for…in goes over property names (the strings «0», «1»…), but we need the values — for…of.

tasks.title: FizzBuzz
tasks.statement: Write a function fizzBuzz(n) that returns an array of n strings for the numbers from 1 to n: «FizzBuzz» for multiples of 15, «Fizz» for multiples of 3, «Buzz» for multiples of 5, otherwise the number itself as a string.
tasks.hint: First check for multiples of 15, then 3 and 5.

tasks.title: A range of numbers
tasks.statement: Write a function range(a, b, step = 1) that returns an array of numbers from a (inclusive) to b (exclusive) with step step; for step > 0 it is an increasing sequence, for step < 0 a decreasing one. For step === 0 throw a RangeError.
tasks.hint: Two loops: for step > 0 the condition is i < b, for step < 0 the condition is i > b.

tasks.title: Sum of digits
tasks.statement: Write a function sumDigits(n): n is a non-negative integer; the function returns the sum of its decimal digits. You must not use strings or arrays — arithmetic only.
tasks.hint: n % 10 is the last digit, Math.floor(n / 10) is the number without it.

tasks.title: Copying an object
tasks.statement: Write a function cloneUser(user) that returns a new object with the same fields, so that changing the copy does not affect the original.
tasks.hint: The spread operator: { ...user }

tasks.title: Change in place or return a new one
tasks.statement: Write two functions. pushIn(list, x) appends x to the end of the array passed in (mutates it) and returns nothing. withItem(list, x) returns a new array with x added, without changing the original.
tasks.hint: push mutates the array, [...list, x] creates a new one.

tasks.title: Safe JSON parsing
tasks.statement: Write a function safeParse(text) that returns { ok: true, value } for valid JSON and { ok: false, error: e.name } if parsing threw an exception.
tasks.hint: try { … JSON.parse … } catch (e) { … e.name … }

tasks.title: Your own exception: division by zero
tasks.statement: Write a function divide(a, b) that returns a / b, and for b === 0 throws a RangeError with the message «Деление на ноль».
tasks.hint: throw new RangeError("Деление на ноль");

tasks.title: The name of an error
tasks.statement: Write a function errorName(fn) that calls fn with no arguments; if fn threw an exception, return its name (the name field), otherwise the string «ok».
tasks.hint: try { fn(); return "ok"; } catch (e) { return e.name; }

tasks.title: Counting types
tasks.statement: Write a function typeCounts(arr) that returns an object where each key is the result of typeof for an element and the value is how many such elements are in the array.
tasks.hint: out[t] = (out[t] ?? 0) + 1

tasks.title: The first defined value
tasks.statement: Write a function firstDefined(arr) that returns the first element of the array that is neither null nor undefined (0, the empty string and false qualify!), or undefined if there is none.
tasks.hint: x != null is the only case where loose comparison is acceptable; or check both values explicitly.

tasks.title: String → number or null
tasks.statement: Write a function parseNum(s) that converts a string to a number with the Number function and returns it; for the empty string, a string of spaces, and anything that gives NaN, it returns null.
tasks.hint: Number("") is 0 — empty strings must be filtered out beforehand.
